conventions.convention: Weights are Lebesgue measurable, locally integrable and positive finite almost everywhere. Their measures are defined on the Lebesgue sigma-algebra and have exactly the Lebesgue null sets; reciprocal powers use an everywhere positive finite representative. Countable Choice is assumed for weighted-space completeness.
Ordinary cubes are open axis-parallel cubes Q(x,r) of side 2r. Dyadic descendants use half-open counterparts, with functions extended across null boundary differences.

For p>1, the A_p characteristic uses cube averages. The A_1 characteristic is the least constant in the uncentred ball inequality M*w ≤ Cw; its cube-average characteristic agrees only up to dimensional factors.
A_infinity is the union of A_p for 1≤p<infinity. The power-decay converse and three-way characterisation assume Dependent Choice.

The weighted singular-integral theorem assumes pointwise kernel size, standard delta-Hölder smoothness, annular cancellation, a principal-value distribution and its L2-bounded convolution operator. These are stronger data than an annular size/Hörmander kernel alone.

The evolution convention is u'=Au, with R(lambda,A)=(lambda I−A) inverse. Sectoriality places a right-opening resolvent sector at omega and a complementary left spectral sector; real operators are complexified before complex resolvents are taken.

Analytic angles lie in (0,pi/2]. Holomorphy is in operator norm away from zero; continuity at zero is strong along every smaller sector. Boundedness is required on every strictly smaller sector, and the maximal angle is a supremum.
The Dunford contour runs inward on the lower ray, through the inner arc from −theta to theta, then outward on the upper ray. Its admissible angle satisfies pi/2+|arg z|<theta<pi/2+delta.

Hilbert pairings and forms are linear in the first variable. The form-associated generator satisfies (Au,v)=−a(u,v). Closedness uses the shifted form norm; its equivalence with a prescribed V norm is obtained under Dependent Choice.

Initial compatibility for the stated classical solution is x∈D(A), with endpoint derivative u'(0)=Ax+f(0); Ax+f(0) is not required to vanish. Higher-order propagation has separately stated graph-norm hypotheses.

Positive-time graph-domain smoothing becomes spatial H^{2m} regularity only after domain identification. The stated bounded-domain identification requires C^{2m} boundary and Delta^j u∈H1_0 for 0≤j<m.
The extremal-cochain inversion set is Phi_w={alpha>0:w inverse alpha<0}, so its root sum is rho−w rho. Exterior covectors have weight −alpha, and the resulting cochain weight is w(lambda+rho)−rho.

The central action on nilradical cohomology factors through the unshifted Harish–Chandra projection. The rho shift enters the Harish–Chandra isomorphism and dot action, not this cohomological action identity.

The Laplacian uses one common Killing-form/Casimir/root-vector normalization, with B(e_alpha,f_alpha)=1, f_alpha=−tau(e_alpha), delta=d*, and a compact-invariant positive Hermitian form. Its scalar assertion concerns weight components actually occurring in the cochain space.

load_bearing.statement: Assume Countable Choice. For 1<p<infinity, w∈A_p when sup_Q average_Q(w) average_Q(w^{−1/(p−1)})^{p−1}<infinity. A_1 instead means M*w≤Cw almost everywhere for some finite C.

A closed densely defined A is sectorial of angle delta∈(0,pi/2] with vertex omega when omega+Sigma_{pi/2+delta}⊂rho(A), and on every smaller stated resolvent sector ||R(lambda,A)||≤M_epsilon/|lambda−omega|.

Assume AC and the stated finite-dimensional complex semisimple, dominant-integral L(lambda), compact-form and common Killing normalization data. Harmonic representatives identify cohomology with ker(square); on each occurring cochain weight component C_mu, square is one half of (||lambda+rho||²−||mu+rho||²) times the identity. The scalar is nonnegative and vanishes exactly for mu∈W·lambda.

Assume AC and the stated complex semisimple data with V=L(lambda), lambda dominant integral. For each w, gamma_w is a nonzero cocycle of weight w·lambda; C^q_{w·lambda}=0 for q≠length(w), and C^{length(w)}_{w·lambda}=C gamma_w. If mu=eta−sum(S) has ||mu+rho||=||lambda+rho||, then uniquely mu=w·lambda, S=Phi_w and eta=w lambda.

Assume Countable Choice. For 1≤p<infinity and w∈A_p, the stated gamma>0 and finite C give (average_Q w^{1+gamma})^{1/(1+gamma)}≤C average_Q w for every cube, with constants controlled by n,p,K_p and the fixed alpha∈(0,1).

Assume DC. In the contour-construction setting, T(0)=I, T(z1+z2)=T(z1)T(z2) for z1,z2∈Sigma_delta, and T(z)x→x along every smaller sector. For x∈D(A), ||T(z)x−x||≤C_{delta',r}|z| ||Ax|| when |z|≤r. Thus T is a bounded analytic semigroup.
Assume DC. For A sectorial at vertex zero and its contour semigroup, every t>0 and m≥1 satisfy T(t)X⊂D(A^m), ||A^mT(t)||≤C_m t^{−m}, and the mth operator-norm time derivative is A^mT(t).

Assume Countable Choice. For 1≤p<infinity, w∈A_p and |k(y)|≤A1|y|^{−n}, every f∈L^p(w), x and epsilon>0 have an absolutely convergent kernel-tail integral, bounded by C A1 w(Q(x,epsilon))^{−1/p}||f||_{L^p(w)}; fixed truncations are Borel measurable.

Assume Countable Choice and the stated standard convolution-kernel/operator and everywhere-finite tail hypotheses. For U=T** or T*, when its level set {Uf>lambda} is proper and open, each Whitney cube satisfies |Q_j∩{Uf>2lambda}∩{Mf≤gamma lambda}|≤C gamma(A1+A2'+A3+B)|Q_j| for the stated small gamma.

Assume DC, the stated analytic semigroup bounds and f∈C^alpha([0,b],X), 0<alpha<1. The two Duhamel pieces lie in D(A), with Av1 equal to the cancelled generator integral and ||Av1(t)||≤c1[f]_alpha t^alpha/alpha, and Av2(t)=(T(t)−I)f(t). Their sum is graph-continuous on [0,b], with Av(0)=0.

Assume AC. For every Lie algebra a over a field k, every a-module V and every n≥0, H^n(a,V) is naturally isomorphic to balanced Ext^n_{U(a)}(k,V), with supplied resolution data. The locally constructed standard complex U(a) tensor Lambda^q(a) is a free resolution, and its Hom differential is the stated zero-based CE differential.

Assume AC. For finite-dimensional complex semisimple g with the stated triangular decomposition, every U(g)-module V, central z, p≥0 and omega∈H^p(n+,V), multiplication of cochain values by z agrees on cohomology with the Cartan action of pr(z).

Assume DC and the stated closed sectorial form, embedding and form-norm comparison data. Its associated A is closed and densely defined; a_lambda is coercive for Re(lambda)>M; A is sectorial with vertex M for every positive delta<pi/2−theta. B=A−MI generates bounded analytic S and T(z)=e^{Mz}S(z) is generated by A. Coercivity alpha gives ||T(t)||≤exp(−alpha t/kappa²).

concerns.concern: The first paragraph describes the power-weight computation as 'splitting the computation into the local singularity at the origin and the growth at infinity'. In ex-power-weight-a-p-range, both thresholds are local integrability conditions at the origin; the far-ball calculation is uniform and creates no separate infinity threshold. The page should distinguish the near-origin/far-ball proof split from the origin of the two thresholds.

seams_checked.note: Opened the supplier page and the consumed generator, resolvent, orbit, Bochner-calculus, Laplace, Lumer–Phillips and variation-of-constants statements. Complex Laplace parameters are proved locally rather than attributed to the real-parameter supplier.
